chapter: Harlem musicians and the road with Armstrong
title: Subbing for Hodges on Duke Ellington's Cotton Club broadcast
summary: When Hodges's wife was having a baby Holmes took his chair in Ellington's broadcast, and Hodges later told Kirkpatrick the sound was Charlie's, not his.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: What I'm leading up to is the one time at least when his first wife was having a baby, and he asked you to sub for him.
Yeah. Right.
And you made a broadcast.
Yeah, Duke was broadcasting. I didn't make the broadcast. I broadcast in the band, with Duke Ellington's band. It was Duke's band.
And that was at the Cotton Club.
At the Cotton Club, yes.
And on one number you took a solo.
Yeah.
Duke turned around and said "Take it."
Yes. Well, I went out there and played what I knew -- a little bit.
Do you remember what number it was?
No, I really don't. I don't remember the numbers. But it was somethin that I was familiar with. I mean, it didn't mean anything to me then. I knew everything that was being played.
Is that the first and only time that you were with Duke?
That's the only time I sat in his band...
And actually played in the band.
Actually while he was working. This was on a broadcast. Yeah, that's the only time.
And then, the next day, you and Johnny were walking down the street...

Yeah. Johnny and his brother-in-law, Kirkpatrick. The three of us were walking down Lenox Avenue, going around to the Bandbox, the musicians' club. And Kirk and Johnny were talking (Kirkpatrick and Johnny), and Kirk was saying, "I caught the broadcast last night. It sounded damn good" -- telling Johnny how good he sound. And Johnny looked at me and smiled, and Johnny said, "That wasn't me, that was Charlie."
So you had a good laugh at that.

Well, it made me feel good, you know, to have somebody else compliment somebody like Johnny Hodges to tell them they sound good, and he knew himself it wasn't him! [LAUGHS] One thing, he give me the credit for it. "It wasn't me; that was Charlie."
